gap: No result ChatGPT got states that BLUETTI's own store sells the AC180 with 400 W of its panels for less when bought as two parts ($769 AC180+200 W kit + $399 SP200L = $1,168, $1.01/Wh) than as its $1,232 'AC180+2*200W' bundle ($1.07/Wh). None states that the Anker C1000 Gen 2 only draws a full 400 W from a panel running at 29 V or more; below that its input tops out near 28 V × 8.2 A ≈ 230 W.
standout_why: Compared against powersized.com/solar-generator-kits (cited; it lists Anker C1000 Gen 2 + 400 W at $1,349.99 with coupon, $1.32/Wh, 41.1 Wh/lb, and has no AC180 kit), voltandvalley.com (only the Jackery 1000 v2, with a 75%-derate refill of about 3.0 h), stormwatts.com bundle-vs-separate (AC180 + 2×200 W at $949 bundle / $1,297 separate, no voltage or current limits), and our own page ($1,232 for BLUETTI, no split-buy price, no input-current limits). None gives the cheaper two-part BLUETTI price from the maker's store, and none turns the stations' input voltage and current limits into the panel voltage a 400 W panel needs. All of them treat 400 W into a 500–600 W input as automatically full power.
decides: Confirms that both BLUETTI and Anker can take a full 400 W only under a voltage condition, and cuts the BLUETTI row's best price from $1,232 to $1,168 (still about $1.01/Wh against the ALLPOWERS kit's roughly $0.68/Wh on our page, which I could not re-verify today). The value pick stays the same. It adds a buying tip for BLUETTI and a check-the-panel-voltage warning for anyone pairing a 400 W panel with the Anker.

findings.label: Solar input limits
findings.value: 500 W max, 12–60 V Voc, 10 A max
findings.note: Weight on the same page: 'About 35.27 lbs / 16kg'; capacity 1,152 Wh (36 Ah).

findings.label: Panel voltage needed for the full 400 W
findings.note: 400 W ÷ 10 A cap = 40 V. Below that, input is capped at V × 10 A, so the two panels need to run at 40 V or more (likely wired in series) to give their full rating.

findings.label: Fastest possible solar refill, empty to full
findings.note: 1,152 Wh ÷ 400 W = 2.88 h at full panel rating, before charging losses.

findings.note: As written on the page: '11-28v⎓8.2A; 29V-60V⎓14.5A (600W Max)'.

findings.label: Top input from a panel running below 29 V
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Portable Power Station
findings.note: 28 V × 8.2 A = 229.6 W. A 400 W panel needs to run at 29 V or more to use the 14.5 A band (29 V × 14.5 A = 420.5 W).

findings.label: Fastest possible solar refill, empty to full
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 Portable Power Station
findings.note: 1,024 Wh ÷ 400 W = 2.56 h at full panel rating, before losses. At the 230 W low-voltage cap: 1,024 ÷ 230 = 4.5 h.

findings.note: 1,024 Wh ÷ 24.9 lb net = 41.1. Page also says the 400 W bundle ships in early December and the single unit from November 21.
